# Equalizer APO vs FXSound: Two Free Windows Equalizers, Two Philosophies
**The short verdict:** pick **Equalizer APO** (with the free Peace GUI) if you want to tune exact frequencies, load a measurement-based profile for your specific headphone, or do room correction. Pick **FXSound** if you want to install it, click a preset, and be done in five minutes. Neither costs a cent, so try both and keep the one that fits how your brain works.

## Quick comparison: at a glance
|  | Equalizer APO | FXSound |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Price | Free, open source (GPL v2) | Free, open source (AGPL v3.0) |
| EQ type | Parametric, unlimited filters, any Fc/gain/Q | 9-band graphic EQ + house presets |
| Interface | Text file; excellent with free Peace GUI | Polished out of the box |
| Learning curve | Real: device selection, restart, “Install as” | Install, pick a preset, done |
| Sound processing | Pure EQ (plus VST if you add it) | EQ + dynamics, bass, ambience, fidelity |
| Room correction (REW) | Yes, reads REW exports directly | No |
| AutoEQ headphone profiles | 500+ models via ParametricEQ.txt | Not supported |
| VST plugins | Yes, system-wide | No |
| Install size | \~10 MB | \~71 MB |
| ASIO / WASAPI exclusive | No | No — same limitation |
| Survives Windows updates | Detaches sometimes; 30-second re-tick fix | Generally unaffected |
| CPU cost | Very low (0.2–0.3 ms measured) | Low |

## Choose this if…
| If you… | Choose |
| --- | --- |
| Own a headphone with an AutoEQ profile | Equalizer APO |
| Want to tune one exact frequency (e.g. an 8 kHz IEM peak) | Equalizer APO |
| Want to correct your room with a measurement mic | Equalizer APO |
| Want it working in five minutes with zero reading | FXSound |
| Like a fuller, louder “enhanced” sound out of the box | FXSound |
| Are setting this up on a non-technical person’s PC | FXSound |
| Need different EQ per app at the same time | Neither — that’s paid Boom 3D |

## Best for: by user type
**Beginners** — start with FXSound. It removes every friction point and you’ll immediately know if its house sound suits you. Graduate to Equalizer APO only when you want more control.

**Audiophiles** — Equalizer APO, no contest. Parametric precision, AutoEQ profiles, and REW room correction are the whole reason the tool exists, and none of it is possible in FXSound.

**Gamers** — Equalizer APO for competitive FPS, because you can build a footstep-clarity curve that boosts the exact 3–6 kHz band; see the tested FPS preset. FXSound if you just want louder, punchier game audio without tuning.

# FxSound and Equalizer APO sound much worse than myHP Audio Control
The problem is it's inside the myHP app... I hate bloat, and this thing seems to cause performance issues (along with HP Support Assistant, HP Analytics, OMEN Gaming, etc.).  However, neither Equalizer APO, nor FxSound come *even close* to the sound quality the silly myHP app manages to produce.

The resultant sound, while markedly better than OOB, is distorted on top of being both quieter and duller compared to myHP's, no matter how much I play around with them. Both programs also make the speakers crackle (both with Audio Enhancements on and off). What did HP/B&O do that dedicated EQ programs couldn't?
To add insult to injury, the app doesn't even offer EQ export, so I'll have to screenshot this and redo the sliders manually.

## SilentIyAwake
This is because they don't have the fine tuning control of a parametric EQ in order to prevent gain in other frequencies from adjusting just one, and no way to "Smoothen" anything.

### hankpeggyhill
To be clear, when I say neither comes even close, I mean it's night and day. Not "this frequency could be lower" but "this sound might as well be coming from different hardware." Not only is it louder and much fuller, but I can hear things I couldn't hear otherwise (unless wearing headphones).

# FxSound Download
## Advantages and Disadvantages
- Exclusively available for Windows PC operating systems.
- May cause device switching or routing glitches.
- Audio latency can disrupt time-sensitive tasks.
- Aggressive settings can distort natural sound quality.
- Lacks advanced filter chains for audio professionals.
- Equalizer APO offers far more deep customization.

## Our Review About FxSound
FxSound is worth trying if you use Windows and want a free, straightforward way to improve or reshape system-wide audio without learning a complex professional equalizer. It can make music, movies, games, and everyday playback sound louder, fuller, clearer, or better balanced, but it is not a universal sound-quality upgrade.

### FxSound Review: Quick Verdict
FxSound is one of the easier options for Windows users who want system-wide EQ, volume enhancement, bass control, presets, and audio effects without paying for an audio enhancer. Its strongest advantage is accessibility: you can begin with a preset and hear the effect immediately, then move into more detailed EQ and DSP controls as needed. Current FxSound also gives considerably more EQ flexibility than older reviews suggest, including an adjustable 5-to-31-band equalizer.

### What Are the Main Drawbacks of FxSound?
#### Specialized Audio Workflows May Need More Control
Users who need complex filter chains, per-channel processing, VST support, room-correction integration, or extremely granular configuration may find Equalizer APO more appropriate. Its official project supports virtually unlimited filters, multiple channels, VST plugins, and integration with Room EQ Wizard.

### FxSound vs Equalizer APO: Which Type of User Should Choose Each?
Equalizer APO's official project supports parametric and graphic equalization, virtually unlimited filters, VST plugins, multiple channels, low CPU use, and Room EQ Wizard integration.

FxSound's advantage is not having more technical capability. Its advantage is making the most common listening adjustments easier to reach.

### Who Should Use FxSound?
#### Consider an Alternative If...
**Our final verdict:** FxSound succeeds because it makes system-wide Windows audio adjustment unusually accessible while still offering considerably more EQ control than older versions did. It is not the right tool for every audiophile or professional workflow, but for everyday Windows listening, its combination of free access, presets, DSP effects, and adjustable EQ gives it a strong value proposition.

# Equalizer APO: Download, Setup & Best Settings
The software was fine. I hit the same wall on my first Equalizer APO install: it sat attached to the wrong audio device for 2 days while I blamed the presets. One setting, and no guide I found told me to check it.

## What is Equalizer APO?
### What it does well
Equalizer APO gives you as many filters as you want, anywhere you want them. **Almost no CPU cost.** Filtering audio is cheap; you will not lose frames in a game. **Room correction** via Room EQ Wizard’s filter format, and **system-wide VST plugins** for compressors, limiters, and virtual surround.

### Who shouldn’t
You want one bass slider and zero tinkering (FxSound, which is free, or Boom 3D, which is paid, do that). You need different EQ per app at the same time (Boom 3D can; Equalizer APO cannot). Your listening runs through ASIO or exclusive mode and you refuse to switch. You record with live mic monitoring where every millisecond matters.

## Equalizer APO features
Measured added latency in a loopback test, averaged over 10 runs. Inaudible for music and gaming; even a 6-filter preset keeps total latency under 3 ms.

**<1%** CPU

**Barely touches your CPU**

Filtering audio is cheap. On any processor from the last decade you will not lose a single frame in a game. It runs quietly in the background.

## Equalizer APO vs the alternatives
| Equalizer  | Equalizer APO | FXSound | Boom 3D | Windows built-in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Price | Free | Free | $19.99 | Free |
| Parametric EQ | Yes | No | No | No |
| Filter count | Unlimited | Fixed | Fixed | Fixed |
| Room correction / VST | Yes | No | No | No |
| Per-app EQ | No | No | Yes | No |
| Beginner friendly | With Peace | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| ASIO / WASAPI exclusive | No | No | No | No |
FxSound is the easier choice if you want one slider and preset effects instead of precise EQ. **Boom 3D** earns its $19.99 only if you need per-app EQ, which Equalizer APO genuinely cannot do.

## Equalizer APO FAQ

# FXSound for Windows
## Unlock your creativity with Adobe Stock
### What is the best way to use FXSound?
After installing FXSound, all our media **suddenly sounded better**. The **bass was deeper**, and there was a certain **clarity to the sound**, which you could only expect from high-quality headphones. This is a great product if you want to use it as a means of **boosting the sound quality of your computer**.

### Are there any alternatives?
There are many **free software alternatives** to configure the equalizer settings on your computer. For example, **Equalizer APO** is an open-source alternative that has similar features to FXSound in terms of customizing frequencies and adding bass enhancer functionality. But the downside is that it only works on 32 bit Windows operating systems. The compatibility issues make FXSound a much better choice for those looking for an all-in-one solution.

### Not just louder, but better sound quality
- Pros

  - Automatically optimizes your audio

  - Easy to customize
